key_insight: Accounting for temperature-dependent water properties through corrected integral profile transformations predicts turbulent channel friction and heat transfer within 2% of DNS, except at the lowest Reynolds numbers.
engineering_relevance: Variable-property modeling can improve heated or cooled water-channel predictions where constant-property assumptions and empirical correlations introduce substantial errors.
method: Run DNS of heated and cooled water channels with temperature-dependent viscosity and conductivity.
Map mean velocity and temperature profiles to constant-property profiles using momentum and energy balances.
Calibrate eddy-viscosity and diffusivity corrections on DNS and incorporate them into the Spalart–Allmaras model.
evidence_signal: Across wall temperatures of 277–360 K and wall Prandtl numbers of 2–12, friction changes by −39% to +32% relative to constant-property flow, empirical correlations deviate by up to 26%, and corrected Spalart–Allmaras modeling halves its friction error.
watch_item: The corrections are calibrated on channel-flow DNS, with reduced accuracy at the lowest Reynolds numbers; transfer to other geometries requires validation.
paper_title: Direct numerical simulation of turbulent heat transfer in water with temperature-dependent viscosity and conductivity
